When I'm running on that kind of energy, I am just so hyper-aware of everything. Every single look the shift manager gives me, every time someone walks past my pallets, I just know, I am absolutely certain they are plotting against me. I can see the whole setup so clearly. turns.doctor_question: During those fired-up periods, did your behavior ever cause serious problems at work, at home, or with other people?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, I guess you could say it caused some problems. I mean, at work, it definitely did. It's actually really frustrating to think about, to be honest. Because of the voice telling me to check, and because I knew they were messing with my numbers. So I'd be on the forklift, and I'd stop to recount a pallet, or I'd go back over my whole manifest three or four times, just to be absolutely sure everything was perfect. But my supervisors... they didn't see it that way. They pulled me into the office, and they were like, "You're slowing down the line, you're holding up the trucks," all this stuff. And then they actually took me off the forklift entirely. Can you believe that? They took me off all the safety-sensitive work, like I was some kind of liability, just because I was being thorough! They stuck me on sweeping duty and breaking down cardboard for like two weeks. It was humiliating, especially when I was the one working harder than anyone else in that whole warehouse. 

And then at home... well, my husband, he gets really frustrated. He says when I get like that, when I'm up all night boxing and making lists and talking a mile a minute, he just can't rely on me. Which I think is unfair, because I'm getting so much done! I'm organizing the whole house, I'm doing the church stuff, I'm working extra shifts. But he says I'm so scattered and so intense that he can't even have a normal conversation with me, let alone trust me to handle regular household stuff without turning it into some massive project. He told me last time that he feels like he's just watching a tornado tear through the house and he's just waiting for it to stop. So, yeah, I guess it does cause problems, even if I don't always agree with why people are upset about it. It just feels like nobody can keep up with me, and then they get mad at me for it.
